title: Normalized finite sheaf descent on connected abelian cover towers
statement:
Let $U$ be an affine scheme and let $(X_i\to U)_{i\in I}$ be an inverse system indexed by a small nonempty directed set. Suppose each $X_i$ is nonempty connected affine and finite etale over $U$, and is supplied with an action of a finite abelian group $\Gamma_i$ such that $(x,g)\mapsto(x,gx)$ identifies $\coprod_{\Gamma_i}X_i$ with $X_i\times_UX_i$. Suppose transition morphisms and surjective group transitions are equivariant and compatible with these comparisons. Let $X=\varprojlim_iX_i$ be nonempty connected and a pro-etale covering of $U$, fix a geometric point $z$ of $X$, and put $G=\varprojlim_i\Gamma_i$ with its profinite topology. Suppose the finite-level comparisons induce $X[G]\cong X\times_UX$ [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects], [def-weil-geometric-point], [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. Let $\mathcal L$ be the full category of set sheaves $F$ on $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ such that $F|_{X_i}$ is a constant finite sheaf for some $i$. Write $Q_F$ for the geometric stalk at the image of $z$ [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk], [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf].

There is a unique splitting $\phi_F:F|_X\cong\underline{Q_F}_X$ inducing the identity on the fibre at $z$; it is the pullback of the uniquely normalized splitting at any connected level trivializing $F$. Every map between constant finite sheaves on a nonempty connected scheme is uniquely determined by its map on one geometric fibre. The descent arrow $\mathrm{pr}_2^*F\to\mathrm{pr}_1^*F$, in the normalized labels and the given comparison convention, defines a continuous left $G$-action on $Q_F$, factoring through some $\Gamma_i$. On the whole scheme $X[G]$, that arrow is $(x,g,v)\mapsto(x,g,g\cdot v)$; this is an equality of sheaf arrows, not just of their values at group elements. The action and splitting are independent of the trivializing level. For $F,F'\in\mathcal L$, taking the fibre gives a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{U_{\mathrm{proet}}}(F,F')\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{G}(Q_F,Q_{F'}).$$
All $\phi_F$ are natural in sheaf morphisms. In particular, equivariant fibre maps glue uniquely across $X\to U$ to sheaf maps, also when one fibre is empty. Moreover $\mathcal L$ is exactly the full category of set sheaves $F$ on $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ whose pullback $F|_X$ is a constant finite sheaf: every such $F$ is already constant finite on some $X_i$. Pullbacks use [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image].

source.place: Bhatt-Scholze Lemma 5.1.2, p.34, classical comparison; agent-formulated finite connected cover descent, normalized at a geometric fibre.

proof.text: For each object of the full finite-level category choose its objectwise normalized splitting and continuous action. These choices occur only inside the proposition proof; the public definitions contain no choices from an unproved existence theorem. For a sheaf morphism define its label map by conjugating the actual stalk map with the two fibre bijections. Cancellation proves its value on fibres; injectivity of the target fibre bijection proves the identity and composition laws.

The morphism descent theorem proves equivariance of each such label map, so these object and map assignments form a functor into continuous actions. For an equivariant map use the unique descended sheaf map as a preimage. The existence equation gives map_preimage, and uniqueness gives preimage_map. This constructs FullyFaithful. The objectwise fibre bijections form a natural isomorphism: its naturality is exactly the cancellation equation defining labelMap.

Take the objectwise universal sections as the splitting family. Transport their normalization, uniqueness and finite-level assertions along the equality between Equiv.ofBijective of the fibre isomorphism and the original fibre equivalence. Morphism descent supplies naturality. Construct actionLabels directly from the continuous action, and descentLabel by pairing the unchanged label with the second base projection. The pullback equations give its two projections. The objectwise whole-overlap equation supplies descent.
Supply finite-level completeness using finite-frame descent. It applies to every sheaf, including those with no given finite-level trivialization.

Prove the remaining constant-map fibre assertion directly. Represent finite constants by labelled coproducts. On a connected nonempty scheme a locally constant label is constant, so every global constant-sheaf section is a constant label. Constant labels on any nonempty pointed neighbourhood are injective, by disjointness of coproduct components. Equality of their germs holds on a common pointed refinement by filtered-colimit equality, hence implies equality of the labels. Apply this to the images of each source label under the two maps on the terminal site object. Their labels agree because their stalk maps agree. Naturality restricts the equality to every site object. The sheafification adjunction makes equality on all original constant labels imply equality of the sheaf morphisms. This also handles empty labels without selecting a label.

This is the first split of the descent node created in the Q15 re-split; that review's FIX added the clause '𝓛 = all X-constant-finite sheaves', and Steps 10–11 now prove it. Step-by-step checks: Step 2 (Yoneda + representability + clopen decomposition) gives arrows as locally constant labels, with the empty cases right. Step 3: on connected T, Hom = Map, and the stalk germ calculation is sound. Step 4: the normalized splitting is unique and does not depend on the level. Step 5: I recomputed the ratios on X_i^3 with vertices (x,gx,hgx) and got ρ(hg)=ρ(g)ρ(h), which is a left action exactly because Γ_i is abelian, as assumed. Step 6: the descent arrow is glued on all of X[G] from the clopen cylinders {g_i=a} using 04TQ uniqueness, so it is a real equality of sheaf arrows. Step 7: level independence by restricting along the sections at g. Step 8: G→Γ_k is surjective by lem-galois-inverse-limit-surjective (finite nonempty groups, surjective transitions, directed I), so equivariance gives the cylinder equalities. Step 9: gluing along the singleton cover X→U gives the Hom bijection, empty fibres included. Step 10: the Isom sheaf H restricts to the constant Sym(A) sheaf on X (locally constant pointwise permutations). Step 11: a constant sheaf is ν^*-classical (ν^* preserves the final object and coproducts); BS 5.1.4/5.1.2 continuity holds here because U is affine and X=lim X_i is small, cofiltered and affine-étale; so the trivialization is defined at a finite level, as in Cor. 5.1.5. Small cases checked: trivial tower, Z/2, empty fibre.
